title: Plasma proteomics random forest predicts worsening heart failure in HCM
summary: In a multicentre prospective cohort of 389 patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, plasma levels of 4986 proteins were measured at enrolment. An 11-protein random forest model trained at one institution (n=268) predicted worsening heart failure with an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI 0.76 to 0.98) in a test set from another institution (n=121). Pathway analysis of dysregulated proteins implicated the Ras-MAPK pathway, an association rather than a demonstrated mechanism.
ai_technology: Random forest model on an 11-protein plasma proteomics signature

evidence.tested: External-institution test set (n=121) after training on n=268, AUC 0.87.
evidence.unknown: Mechanism of the pathway association; small cohort; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest selected and combined 11 plasma proteins to predict worsening heart failure.
